aboutH2: Bowline Health: virtual recovery coaching from Calgary
intro: Bowline Health is a Calgary company that offers addiction recovery coaching to adults across Alberta. It is not a rehab and does not treat anyone. Coaches help you plan your recovery, keep you accountable and find the services you need, and Bowline's website is clear that they do not diagnose, give medical advice or provide counselling.

Most coaching happens through Bowline's virtual Recovery Coaching Navigation Centre, by phone or online, on weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. You can also walk in, with no appointment, at navigation centres in Calgary and Edmonton and a Recovery Support Centre in Red Deer. Much of the work is with people waiting for a recovery community bed or coming home from one.

pillars.title: Coaching, not treatment
pillars.body: A Bowline coach is closer to a guide than a clinician. You sit down, by phone or in person, and build a recovery wellness plan with short-term and long-term goals. After that the coach checks in, keeps you to what you agreed and adjusts the plan as things change. Methods come from motivational interviewing and cognitive-behavioural work, and progress is measured every 30 days with the Recovery Capital Index. What a coach will not do is just as clear on Bowline's website: no therapy, no medical advice, no diagnosis and no 12-step sponsorship. If you need those, the coach refers you on.

pillars.title: Help while you wait, and when you come home
pillars.body: Waiting for a bed in a recovery community can be the hardest stretch, and Bowline puts a lot of its coaching there. Coaches stay in contact through the wait, work with health providers to move referrals along and help you get into the program once a spot opens. The same coaches pick people up again when they leave residential treatment, with regular check-ins, help finding housing and work, and introductions to support groups in Calgary, Edmonton, Red Deer or back home in a smaller Alberta town.

pillars.title: A virtual centre and three walk-in sites
pillars.body: Bowline's virtual Recovery Coaching Navigation Centre runs from Calgary and takes calls and messages from anywhere in Alberta, which matters if you live a long way from a city. For face-to-face help there are walk-in sites at 10530 96 Street in Edmonton, at the Salvation Army Centre of Hope on 9th Avenue SE in Calgary's East Village, and at 5239 53 Avenue in Red Deer. None of them needs an appointment, and none of them asks you to be admitted anywhere first.

overviewH2: Bowline Health: how the coaching works
overview: Getting started is simple. You fill in the intake form on bowlinehealth.ca, and Bowline calls you back to match you with a recovery coach who stays your main contact. The form asks whether you live in Alberta, for your health number, whether you are 18 or older and whether you are on a waitlist for treatment or a recovery community. It also asks about medication, opioid agonist treatment and safety, so the coach knows where you are starting from.

From there you can have one-to-one coaching, join group sessions with other people in recovery, or both. Group sessions are run by coaches with lived experience and mix discussion, shared activities and skill-building. Bowline's coaches keep a provincial list of recovery services, from inpatient and outpatient treatment and counsellors to Alberta Health Services primary care, fitness-based recovery programs, and peer, 12-step and land-based groups.

faqIntro: Answers come from Bowline Health's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Bowline Health a rehab or treatment centre?
faqs.a: No. Bowline Health is a recovery coaching service, mostly delivered by phone and online from Calgary, with walk-in coaching in Calgary, Edmonton and Red Deer. It has no beds and offers no detox, therapy or medical care. Its website says coaches do not diagnose or treat conditions and refer people to counsellors, therapists or doctors when they need that kind of help.

faqs.q: What does a Bowline recovery coach actually do?
faqs.a: A coach helps you write a recovery wellness plan, checks in with you regularly and holds you to the goals you set. Coaches also help you find services across Alberta, from inpatient and outpatient treatment to counsellors, housing help, employment services and peer or 12-step groups. They do not act as 12-step sponsors.

faqs.q: How does virtual recovery coaching work?
faqs.a: You fill in the intake form on Bowline's website, and the team calls you back and matches you with a recovery coach who stays your main contact. Coaching then happens by phone or online, one to one or in groups, from home or another safe place. The virtual centre is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: Where can I see a recovery coach in person?
faqs.a: Bowline lists three walk-in sites with no appointments needed. The Edmonton Navigation Centre is at 10530 96 Street and is open weekdays 9 am to 5 pm. The Calgary Navigation Centre is at the Salvation Army Centre of Hope, 420 9th Avenue SE, and the Red Deer Recovery Support Centre is at 5239 53 Avenue, both open weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

Bowline's intake form is set up for Alberta residents aged 18 and over who are looking for help with a substance use disorder. It asks for your Alberta health number. If you live outside Alberta, call 780-666-6223 before applying, because the website does not describe service for other provinces yet.

faqs.q: How much does Bowline Health cost?
faqs.a: Bowline's website does not publish any fees. Its recovery.com listing says the program is offered at no cost and may have eligibility rules or limited spots. Confirm with Bowline when it calls you back after intake.

faqs.q: Can Bowline help while I wait for a treatment bed?
faqs.a: Yes. Supporting people on waitlists for recovery communities and other bed-based programs is one of the main things Bowline does. Coaches stay in touch while you wait, work with health providers on referrals and help you move into the program when a spot opens. Some Alberta recovery communities ask applicants to have a coach, so ask the program you are applying to.

faqs.q: Does Bowline help after residential treatment?
faqs.a: Yes. Bowline describes continuing care for people leaving a structured program such as an inpatient treatment centre. Coaches help with settling back into the community, keep up regular check-ins to lower the risk of relapse and connect you with support groups, housing and job services.

Bowline Health is based in Calgary. Its Google listing gives an office at 5940 Macleod Trail SW, Suite 800, near Chinook Centre, about 10 to 15 minutes by car from downtown. The website does not list this as a walk-in site, so for in-person coaching in Calgary go to the Centre of Hope at 420 9th Avenue SE.

Bowline says its coaches have personal experience of addiction and relapse and use evidence-based methods such as motivational interviewing and goal setting. Through partners in its parent group, the Recovery Coach Academy of Canada and the Recovery Training Institute of Alberta, it runs certification training for recovery coach professionals.
